findings.quote: I assumed the distance grows by a fixed step
findings.note: The entry is the linear count 1, 2, 3, but the correct ratio 1:3:5 also grows by a fixed step (of two), so the phrase does not pin the wrong pattern and reads as true of the right answer as well. A student who tapped it could have meant either, which blurs the diagnosis.
findings.fix: I counted the distances as one, two, three

notes: Types accepted: mistakes[0] concept (equal distances each second is a wrong belief about accelerated motion), mistakes[1] concept (a wrong belief about how the distances grow), mistakes[2] application (the t squared rule is known but applied to totals rather than to each single second - the definition's 'wrong interval'). right_route names the nth-second rule, which none of the three wrong entries uses, so it separates properly. Values re-checked: 5, 15, 25 m, ratio 1:3:5.
